cdp.name: CDP
cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

genai.name: Generative AI
genai.gloss: Models that produce content — copy, images, replies — from a prompt.

agentic.name: Agentic AI
agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO
geo.gloss: Generative Engine Optimization — being visible inside AI answers.

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: AI is making customers expect more and tolerate less
stories.plain: As AI-powered service becomes the norm, customers now expect near-instant, accurate resolutions — and get frustrated faster when they don't get them. The piece argues that speed without resolution and removing easy human escalation paths is backfiring, forcing brands to rethink how they govern AI interactions in customer engagement.

stories.head: Contentstack launches Canoe AI visibility tool at $279/month; Mixpanel adds Agent Intelligence
stories.plain: The daily roundup contains two product launches worth noting: Contentstack's Canoe targets GEO — helping brands track and improve their presence inside AI-generated answers — while Mixpanel's Agent Intelligence adds agentic analytics capabilities. Both signal that vendors are now shipping concrete tools around emerging AI categories.

stories.head: B2B marketing doesn't have an ROI problem — it has an evidence problem
stories.plain: The article argues that B2B marketers can't prove value not because results aren't there, but because they lack connected data across the full buyer journey. Linking CDP-level buyer data to revenue attribution — rather than relying on campaign-level reporting — is framed as the core fix, with direct implications for how AI decisioning tools are evaluated.

stories.head: CommerceIQ brings agentic AI retail media management to Chewy Ads
stories.plain: CommerceIQ is extending its agentic bid and budget optimization to Chewy's retail media network, letting pet brands automate campaign performance decisions in real time. This matters because it shows agentic decisioning moving beyond the major retail media players into specialist marketplaces, broadening where brands need AI governance.

stories.head: Mixbook CEO: why AI-powered personalization never mentions AI in customer messaging
stories.plain: Mixbook's Andrew Laffoon explains how the brand uses AI to personalize photo-book creation while keeping the customer as the perceived author — deliberately hiding the AI layer. He argues NPS and emotional resonance outrank speed as success metrics, offering a practical model for ethical AI-assisted personalization.

stories.head: ZoomInfo Introduces Agent Teams, Powered by Acquisition of DoubleO.ai
stories.plain: ZoomInfo acquired DoubleO.ai and launched Agent Teams, a product that coordinates multiple AI agents across a company's systems to run complete go-to-market plays — from detecting a buying signal all the way to taking action — without human babysitting. This shifts agentic AI from single-task tools to orchestrated, multi-agent GTM execution, which is a meaningful buying and build decision for revenue teams.

stories.head: Contentstack Launches Canoe, an AI Visibility Tool Showing Brands What AI Tells Their Buyers
stories.plain: Contentstack's new standalone product, priced at $279/month, audits how a brand is named, described, and cited inside AI-generated answers, benchmarks it against up to ten competitors, and outputs a ranked fix list that AI agents can act on. It is one of the first commercially available GEO measurement tools at an accessible price point, making it relevant for both buyers and builders in martech.

stories.head: Jellyfish Research: AI Shopping Assistants Create Radically Different 'AI Shelves,' Upending Brand and Price Rules
stories.plain: Jellyfish research shows that AI shopping assistants surface a completely different competitive set than traditional search, meaning established brand leaders and price anchors don't carry over. Brandtech also launched a 'Share of Model' measurement product tied to this finding. Marketers now need new metrics and optimization strategies just to stay visible in AI-mediated purchase decisions.

stories.head: DataDome Joins Experian Agent Trust Ecosystem to Add Continuous Intent Verification to Agentic Commerce
stories.plain: As AI agents increasingly make purchases and decisions on behalf of consumers, Experian and DataDome are building infrastructure to verify not just who an agent represents, but whether its live actions stay within what it was authorized to do. This is a foundational governance layer for agentic commerce — directly relevant to anyone buying or building autonomous marketing and shopping systems.

stories.head: Mixpanel Introduces Agent Intelligence to Connect AI Agent Conversations to Business Outcomes
stories.plain: Mixpanel's new Agent Intelligence module links what AI agents say in conversations directly to downstream customer behavior and revenue outcomes. This closes a critical measurement gap — until now, teams could build agents but couldn't reliably tell which agent interactions actually drove results. It matters for anyone responsible for proving ROI on agentic AI investments.

themes.head: The AI Search Takeover Rewrites Brand Visibility Rules
body: AI-powered search engines and shopping assistants are now filtering brand narratives before a human ever sees them — meaning your SEO strategy, pricing story, and brand positioning are being summarized, reranked, or dropped entirely by LLMs. New research from Jellyfish confirms this is already upending brand leadership & competitive dynamics in ways traditional search never did.

Vendors are racing to give marketers a window into this black box: Contentstack's Canoe tool, for instance, shows brands exactly what AI tells their buyers. The strategic decision is no longer just 'rank higher' — it's 'earn a citation inside the AI answer.' Visual SEO and generative-engine optimization are now distinct disciplines marketers must master.
ev: MarTech Series · Jellyfish AI shopping research
MarTech · Visual SEO for AI search

themes.head: Agentic AI Sprawl Becomes a Governance Crisis
body: Go-to-market teams are deploying AI agents faster than they can inventory them — and the resulting sprawl is creating accountability gaps, duplicated spend, and unmeasured risk. ZoomInfo's acquisition of DoubleO.ai to launch 'Agent Teams,' and Mixpanel's new Agent Intelligence layer, both signal that the market knows orchestration & measurement of agents is the next unsolved problem.

Trust infrastructure is emerging as a parallel necessity: DataDome joining Experian's Agent Trust ecosystem for 'continuous intent verification' shows that agentic commerce needs identity guardrails the same way human commerce needed fraud detection. IBM's self-hosted AI sovereignty play points the same direction — enterprises want control, not just capability.
ev: MarTech · GTM teams losing track of agents

themes.head: AI Made Marketing Faster, Not Better — and the Gap Is Showing
body: A candid thread running through this month's commentary is that speed gains from AI have outpaced quality gains — content is cheaper to produce but not more persuasive, and customers now expect more while tolerating less. The MarTech piece 'AI is making customers expect more and tolerate less' frames this as a trust & experience crisis, not just a content problem.

The skill-gap data reinforces it: job postings are demanding AI proficiency, but they are increasingly specifying judgment, editing, and strategic oversight — not just prompt-writing. Mixbook's CEO deliberately avoids saying 'AI' in customer messaging, betting that permanence & craft matter more to buyers than automation speed.
ev: Agile Brand · Mixbook designing for permanence

themes.head: The B2B Buyer Journey Has Been AI-Shaped — CMOs Aren't Ready
body: B2B buyers are now doing more research through AI assistants before ever contacting sales, which means the classic demand-gen funnel assumptions — who touches what, when, and why — are breaking down. Circle & Square's buyer intelligence guide and the Salesforce acquisition of Listen Labs (an AI customer research startup) both point to the same gap: marketers lack real-time evidence of how & where AI is shaping purchase intent.

The ROI attribution problem is actually an evidence problem, as MarTech argues this month — teams can't prove marketing works because they can't see the AI-mediated interactions that precede conversion. Growth7's platform turning CRM data into pipeline action is a direct commercial response: close the evidence gap or lose budget.
ev: MarTech Series · Growth7 CRM to pipeline

themes.head: Retail & CTV Media Face AI-Driven Reinvention of Timing & Targeting
body: AI is compressing & redistributing retail purchase windows: the holiday calendar has effectively been rewritten by algorithmic deal discovery & AI shopping agents, but most retailers are still running last decade's seasonal playbook. CommerceIQ's expansion into Chewy Ads shows AI-powered retail media management is moving beyond Amazon into every major marketplace, demanding real-time optimization at scale.

Connected TV is undergoing a parallel transformation — Comcast research now maps how TV & streaming drive results across the full buyer journey, not just awareness, while Jamloop's Verified Supply initiative tackles the transparency & accountability gap that has long plagued CTV. The convergence of shoppable media, AI bidding, and journey attribution is forcing a fundamental rebuild of how retail & media budgets are planned together.
ev: MarTech Series · Comcast TV buyer journey research

month.takeaway: Every major shift this month orbits the same core tension: AI is accelerating marketing execution while simultaneously eroding the visibility, trust, and evidence marketers need to prove it's working — and the vendors, platforms, and strategies gaining traction are precisely those that close that gap.
